analysis:
Examined the new selected-model recovery implementation and all supplied Serve.swift metadata, patch and base excerpts. Recovery adds background residency work affecting A-018, TB-007/T-029 and TB-012/T-059. Selected targets are filtered by advertised status, runtime eligibility, retirement and self-test fences (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift:35-42). Planning protects ordinary selections and pins, considers eviction exclusions and dwell/idle/lease limits, and rechecks victims before unloading (78-122, 176-242, 273-288). Loads use ensureModelLoaded with eviction disabled (295); memory arithmetic saturates rather than wrapping. Drain and concurrent-residency checks are present (151-162). No independently supported security regression was identified in this scope.
Serve.swift head:497 adds recovery to existing cancellation/bounded-wait shutdown handling; head:523 replaces inline teardown with unloadAllModelsForShutdown. Registration, fixed process-key binding, connection-authorization invalidation and separate attestation dispatch in the supplied base surrounding source are unchanged (base:181-225, 410-448), with no observed change to A-001 encryption, A-008 tokens, A-016 authorization, billing or T-041 cache isolation/at-rest controls.
Integration must verify the changed teardown helper preserves unload completion and native-owner safety; its implementation is not supplied here. Also trace recovery's capacity-tick/enqueue wiring, cancellation/backoff state and adoption release, plus ensureModelLoaded/unloadModel contracts: after planning or unload suspensions, final load admission must enforce add-on holds, drain, retirement/self-test fences and concurrent placements, and eviction must protect active requests. Relevant new call sites are recovery:134-145 and 279-295. These are unverified cross-file contracts, not evidence of missing controls. Only selected threat definitions were supplied in full; unchanged dependencies were not examined.
